name: Vasuki indicus

features.claim: It was very long, with an estimated body length between 10.9 and 15.2 metres.
features.quote: It has an estimated body length between 10.9–15.2 m (36–50 ft), making it the largest known madtsoiid.

features.claim: Its body was slightly smaller in its vertebral dimensions than Titanoboa's.
features.quote: Although the vertebral dimensions of Vasuki are slightly smaller than those of Titanoboa (estimated at 12.8 m (42 ft) ± 2.2 m (7 ft 3 in)), the upper length estimates indicate a longer body for the former.

second_reading.quote: Vasuki indicus is an extinct snake species in the family Madtsoiidae that lived during the Middle Eocene in India.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: It had vertebrae, and 27 of them from before the cloaca were found.
second_reading.quote: The specimen consists of 27 pre-cloacal vertebrae, some of which were found in articulation.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Its body was probably not suited to living in water, but to living on land or partly in water.
second_reading.quote: Unlike other large-bodied snakes like Titanoboa, Vasuki was probably not an aquatic animal.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The shape of its vertebrae suggests it lived on land, or possibly partly in water.
second_reading.quote: Its vertebral morphology instead suggests a terrestrial (or possibly semi-aquatic) lifestyle when compared to related madtsoiids and modern pythonoids.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: It is not certain whether a second vertebra found belongs to a second species of Vasuki or is just a difference between males and females.
second_reading.quote: However, multiple characters also distinguish the vertebra from the Vasuki indicus holotype, suggesting it may be a second distinct species in the genus. Alternatively, the differences could be explained by sexual dimorphism within the species.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it
